full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel, J: This Rule Nisi, under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Gazette Notification No.31.00.0000.045- .53.005. 2012-2782 dated 29-11-2012, issued by the respondent No.2 relating to serial No. 8 Khatian Nos.17, 07 and 58 of Mouza-204 Hashdi and serial No.04 Khatian No.370 of Mouza 203 Batoia within Upozila Kabirhat, District-Noakhali showing it in 'ka' list of Orpita Shompatty in page No.2012 of Bangladesh Gazette (Extra Copy) published on 5-12-2012 (Annexure-F) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, as stated in the writ petition, in short, are that the Sokhomoy and Makhonmoy were owners of 16.51 acres of land of MRR Khatian No.17 corresponding to CS Khatian No.16 and land of MRR Khatian No.7 corresponding to CS Khatian No.9 and lands of MRR Khatian No.35 corresponding to CS Khatian No.20 of Mouza Hashdi under Upozila Sadar at present Kabirhat within District-Noakhali. Shishu Bala, wife of Sokhomoy, was the owner of lands of MRR Khatian 52 corresponding to CS Khatian No.34 of the said Mouza. Noni Gopal Sen was the owner of lands of MRR Khatian No.33 corresponding to CS Khatian No.70 of the said Mouza. Shishu Bala Rai Choudhurani was the owner of lands of MRR Khatian No.370 corresponding to CS Khatian No.318 of the Mouza Batoia within Upozila Sadar at present Kabirhat within District-Noakhali and their names were recorded in the said MRR Khatians. Sokhomoy and Makhonmoy were the owners of 17 decimals of land of MRR Khatian 336 corresponding to CS Khatian No.285 of Mouza Batoia. They were also owners of 43 decimals of land of MRR Khatian 116 corresponding to CS Khatian No.91 of Mouza Batoia. The MRR Khatians were prepared in their names. Thus, the said persons were owners of 12.351/2 acres of land. They exchanged their lands with one Abul Kalam of Tripura State of India. Sukhomoy and others appointed one Selamot Ulla as their attorney for the purpose of the said exchange by swearing affidavit before the Magistrate of Bilonia of Tripura. The Magistrate authenticated it on 13-9-1963 and Divisional Commissioner, Chattogram validated it on 3-12-1963. Then, Abul Kalam appointed one Profolla Kumar Mojumdar as his attorney on 13-9-1963 and the said Attorney executed and registered deed in favour of Sukhomoy and others accordingly. 

 3. Selamot Ullah, Attorney of Sukhomoy and others executed and registered deed Nos. 2551, 2552 and 2553 in favour of Abul Kalam on 30-4-1977. Thereafter, as Abul Kalam was in service abroad, he appointed Kala Miah as his Attorney vide registered Power of Attorney No.1907 dated 23-2-1985. Thereafter, Kala Miah also sold 15 decimals of land to Rahamat Ullah vide registered deed No.4967 dated 6-9-1987, who sold it to petitioner No.6 vide registered saf kabala 5250 dated 17-12-1988 and Kala Miah also gifted 18 decimals of land to the petitioner No.9 vide registered deed of gift No.3819 dated 4-8-1988. Kala Miah also sold 1.16 acres to Tarifa Khatun vide registered saf kabala No.5051 dated 13-1-1987 and on her death, it was inherited by her heir petitioner No. 10. Further, Abul Kalam sold 361/2 decimals to Abdul Khalek, Shofiullah and Siddique Ullah vide registered saf kabala dated 13-10-1979. The petitioners Nos. 11-13 are heirs of Abdul Khalek and petitioners No.14 and 15 are heirs of Siddique Ullah and petitioner No.16 is heir of Shofi Ullah. In this way, the petitioners are owners of 12.951/2 acres of land and the Khatian was opened in their names and they paid rent regularly. The petitioners have their homestead at plot No. 156 and 139. 

 8. Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners at the very outset by referring all the annexures chronologically submits that the petitioners are the legal owners and possessor of the case property, the Khatian was opened in their names and they paid rent regularly. They have their homestead at plot No.156 and 139 and they never left the country and have been enjoying the said property since long. He further submits that the property in question as shown in impugned Gazette notification dated 5-12-2012 was never a vested property and it was never been leased out to anybody. It was wrongly included in the list of vested property and, as such, the impugned Gazette notification is without any lawful authority. 

 15. In the present writ petition, the main cause of the petitioners to file this writ petition is that a Gazette Notification was published, wherein the petitioners’ properties have been enlisted as vested property. After careful perusal of the records, it appears that the petitioners are owners of total 12.951/2 acres of land. The Khatians were also opened in their names and they paid rent regularly. It further appears that the petitioners have their homestead at plot No.156 and 139. From the above facts and circumstances, it is clear that the petitioners name have been recorded in the record of right, they paid rent, never left the country and had been enjoying the said property since long from their purchase. From the RS record, it shows clearly the names of the petitioners as the owner of the property in question and not the Government. Now, in respect of the issue of maintainability of the present writ petition, the present writ petition is very much maintainable. For invoking writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution, the petitioners do not require to show any alternative efficacious remedy. In this connection, the view of our Apex Court has been decided in the case of Government of Bangladesh, represented by Ministry of Works vs Syed Chand Sultana, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 24. It has been held that:-"The writ petitioners can come directly to the High Court Division for protection of their fundamental right even though an alternative remedy is available."
